name: Eyelid tape / fold stickers

lead: Eyelid tape and fold stickers are small, often crescent-shaped adhesive strips placed on the upper lid so the skin folds into a visible crease. People with single (monolid) lids use them for a double eyelid look without surgery, and looksmaxxers also use them to lift hooded or drooping lids.

The effect lasts as long as the strip stays on. Research is limited to a few small studies and reports: a 2020 study looked at the front surface of the eye after four weeks of wear in young women with single eyelids, a case series described tape holding up a drooping lid in myotonic dystrophy type 1, and a 2025 paper reviewed long-term use.

paras: The strip sticks to the lid skin and holds a fold above the lash line, imitating the crease a levator attachment forms naturally. It is applied daily, often under or alongside makeup, and removed at night. It is the non-surgical counterpart to double eyelid surgery.

Skin irritation from adhesives and repeated lid stretching are the concerns most often mentioned in the cosmetic and plastic surgery literature. Eyelid tape is a cosmetic product sold without prescription in most markets.

chain: Double eyelid or more open eye
angle.text: Eyelid tape and fold stickers create a temporary upper-lid crease, giving a double eyelid look or a more open eye straight away. They are removable and are the non-surgical counterpart to double eyelid surgery. Small studies have looked at effects on the eye surface after weeks of wear.

lead: Eyelid tape, also sold as fold stickers or double eyelid tape, consists of thin adhesive strips applied to the upper eyelid to create a temporary crease. Many East Asians use the product to produce a double eyelid effect as a temporary means of increasing perceived beauty [1]. It is the non-surgical counterpart to double eyelid surgery, which creates a permanent crease in people who do not have one naturally [2].

In looksmaxxing communities the tape is discussed both as a way to simulate a double eyelid and as a stopgap for droopy or hooded lids, including mild ptosis [3]. Published research is limited: a small study examined ocular surface health after four weeks of wear [1], a clinical report has described the tape as an option for severe ptosis in myotonic dystrophy [4], and a 2025 article in Aesthetic Plastic Surgery discusses long-term use [5].
infobox: Adhesive strips applied to the upper eyelid
Temporary double eyelid or lid lift
Cosmetic product in most markets; not specified in sources

paras: Eyelid tape is sold in rolls or as pre-cut strips, often in a thin crescent or sickle shape, that adhere to the skin of the upper lid. When the wearer opens the eye, the strip pushes the skin above it into a fold that resembles a natural supratarsal crease [1].

A double eyelid is an upper lid with a visible crease. Surveys summarised on Wikipedia report that the crease is naturally present in about 41% of Koreans and roughly 70 to 83% of Chinese and Japanese people [2]. Surgical creation of the crease is described as one of the most commonly performed cosmetic procedures in Taiwan and South Korea, and the first recorded operation is credited to Dr. Kotaro Mikamo in Japan in 1896 [2]. Tape and stickers are used by people who want the appearance without surgery.

On looksmax.org, eyelid tape appears in threads about drooping eyelids. One poster suggests tape as a fallback for "mild ptosis on random days" when other home measures they describe do not work, while acknowledging that they have no proof for their suggested routine [3].

Forum users in such threads tend to frame hooded or droopy lids as a lost opportunity for a more open, alert eye area, and tape as the cheapest reversible option. These are community views rather than published findings [3].

The adhesive sits next to the eye and is pressed against the lid margin region. In a 2020 study, researchers examined the front of the eye in young women with single eyelids who wore double eyelid tape for four weeks, looking at blinking and ocular surface measures [1]. A separate 2025 paper in Aesthetic Plastic Surgery addresses the implications of long-term use [5].
Medical tape is also used in other clinical contexts, such as taping eyelids closed during anaesthesia to protect the cornea [6]. That use is unrelated to cosmetic fold creation.

A 2020 study in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health recruited 29 young adult women with single eyelids and examined anterior ocular health, including blinking characteristics and ocular surface health, over four weeks of double eyelid tape wear [1].

A 2022 report in the American Journal of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation described double eyelid tape as a treatment option for severe ptosis in patients with myotonic dystrophy type 1, a condition in which the levator muscle is often affected and surgery may be considered infeasible [4].
A 2025 article in Aesthetic Plastic Surgery discusses the implications of long-term double eyelid tape use [5]. No randomized trials of tape for appearance outcomes were found.

lore.intro: Eyelid tape is discussed in looksmaxxing forums mainly as a cheap, reversible way to open up hooded or droopy lids [3].
